set.requirements: USD 52.7bn over five years for Commerce semiconductor programmes [CLM-0311], of which USD 39bn manufacturing incentives and USD 11bn R&D [CLM-0312]; plus up to USD 75bn loan authority backed by USD 6bn of the 39bn [@oig_total, @gao_loansub]; eligible 'covered entities' include fabrication, assembly, test, advanced packaging, materials and equipment facilities [CLM-0024]; awards move from nonbinding PMT to final direct funding agreement and are disbursed as reimbursements on verified milestones, with clawbacks [@oig_pmt, @gao_reimburse]. First NOFO: direct funding generally 5-15% of capex, total incl. loans up to 35%, max USD 3bn per project without extra certification [@gao_nofo_range]; upside sharing required above USD 150m [@gao_upside_rule]; childcare requirements removed by 2025-26 amendments [@gao_amend14]; dividend and buyback limits (e.g. Micron) [@mu_conditions]. Status: 19 companies / 40 projects, USD 30.9bn direct funding + USD 5.5bn loans awarded by July 2025 [@gao_awards]; USD 6bn disbursed by July 2025 [@gao_disbursed] plus USD 5.695bn accelerated to Intel in Aug 2025 in exchange for equity [@intc_close]; 12 PMTs incl. Wolfspeed USD 750m still unfinalised June 2026 [@crs_pending]; no awards publicly rescinded as of July 2026 [@crs_norescind]; 14 awards amended Jan 2025-Apr 2026 [@gao_amend14]. R&D: USD 7.8bn of USD 11bn in awards cancelled (Natcast NSTC, SRC SMART USA, NAPMP), USD 506.8m expended; replaced by an equity-seeking BAA [@gao_rd_cancel, @gao_rd_spent, @baa_equity]. After March 2025 the CPO sits under the US Investment Accelerator [CLM-0316, @oig_accel]. FY2026 is the last year of advance appropriations for incentives [@crs_fy26].

set.penalties: Expansion clawback: recovery of up to the full award if a recipient materially expands (more than 5% of capacity via added cleanroom, line or space) semiconductor capacity in a foreign country of concern within 10 years; existing legacy facilities may expand 10% over 10 years [@gr_material]. Technology clawback: full award recovered for knowing joint research or technology licensing with a foreign entity of concern on national-security-relevant technology [@gr_tech]. Parallel 48D recapture of 100% of credits [@recapture]. No post-2023 amendment found [@gr_nochange].

set.requirements: Investment tax credit for facilities whose primary purpose is making semiconductors or semiconductor manufacturing equipment; 35% for property placed in service after 2025 (25% before) following P.L. 119-21 [CLM-0278, CLM-0315, @irs_rates]; qualified property is tangible depreciable property integral to the facility, excluding office/administrative buildings [@irs_bldg]; no credit for construction beginning after 31 Dec 2026 [CLM-0280, @crs_itc_deadline], construction start shown by physical work or 5% safe harbor [@boc]; elective (direct) payment with IRS pre-filing registration [CLM-0281, @irs_reg]; 10-year recapture for material expansion in a foreign country of concern [@recapture]. Scored at USD 24.3bn over 2022-2031 at enactment [@cbo_48d]; no official estimate of the 35% increase found [@cost35_unknown]. NIST's fact sheet and some filings still say 25% (CON-0009) [CLM-0367, @tsmc_25itc]. Industry seeks extension beyond 2026 [@semi_ext]; none enacted as of Sept 2026 [@ext_unknown].

set.remaining_uncertainty: Rate question settled by IRS page (updated 27 Jul 2026): 25% for property placed in service through 2025, 35% thereafter. Company filings (TSMC 20-F FY2025, Intel Nov 2024) still describe 25%, probably reflecting pre-2026 assets or pre-amendment wording. Open: whether the 31 Dec 2026 construction deadline is extended (not enacted as of Sept 2026; see res-RU-0026-0f93).

set.resolving_evidence: GAO-26-109121 confirms 14 awards amended Jan 2025-Apr 2026 (childcare removed, 2 equity deals incl. Intel, upside sharing removed for 2 projects); still needed: identity of the second equity/warrant awardee and per-award changes to milestones and amounts.
